original_value: SummaryCooperative nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system is an effective solution for the fifth generation (5G) wireless mobile communications systems. In this work, the achievable rate analysis of a NOMA communication network with decode‐and‐forward (DF) relaying under κ‐μ shadowed fading conditions is investigated. First, we develop an analytical framework for cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the considered system model. Then, the average achievable rate expressions for two different information bits namely s1 and s2 are derived based on the derived CDF for NOMA with DF relaying over κ‐μ shadowed fading channels. Furthermore, we also propose simplified average achievable rate expressions for the special cases of κ‐μ shadowed fading channels in order to facilitate the evaluation of the derived expressions. Some numerical examples on the achievable rate of the considered system are shown for different scenarios. Moreover, our derived analytical average achievable rate expressions are confirmed by the simulations results.

This work examines achievable-rate analysis of a NOMA communication network with decode-and-forward (DF) relaying over κ-μ shadowed fading conditions. First, an analytical framework is developed for the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the system model considered. Then, using the derived CDF, average achievable-rate expressions for the two information bits s1 and s2 are obtained for NOMA with DF relaying over κ-μ shadowed fading channels. In addition, simplified average achievable-rate expressions are proposed for special cases of κ-μ shadowed fading channels to ease evaluation of the derived formulas. Several numerical examples illustrating the achievable rate of the considered system are presented for different scenarios. The derived analytical average achievable-rate expressions are also validated by simulation results.
